findings.title: PermDenialCache can block legitimate access after permission grant or resource recreation
findings.body: The permDenialCache is consulted at the very start of Check() (lines 116-121) and short-circuits to Allowed:false without ever touching the DB or the permCache. The denial is written at lines 153-155 whenever checkPermission returns false, with a 30-second TTL (shortCacheTTL). Because the denial entry is never invalidated when permissions change or resources are created, the following scenarios keep a freshly-authorised user locked out for up to 30 seconds: (1) user A previously failed a check on resource X (e.g. before X existed or before the grant), the entry is cached, then X is created with A as owner / A is added to a team that grants access — the next Check still hits the denial key and denies; (2) the same happens when a resource is deleted and later recreated with the same UID under new ownership; (3) a race where A asks for X before the create-grant transaction commits — A is denied, the denial is cached, and once the transaction commits A still cannot access X until the entry expires. This re-introduces precisely the 'creator cannot access the dashboard/folder they just created' symptom this PR is supposed to fix. Consider only caching denials for resources known to exist, invalidating the entry on permission change, or dropping the TTL drastically.

findings.title: List does not fall back to DB when the permCache is stale, leaving newly created items invisible
findings.body: In the new List() the only DB fallback is on a complete cache miss (getCachedIdentityPermissions returns cache.ErrNotFound). If the user already has a populated permCache for the action, List trusts it as-is and never requeries. Compare with Check() (lines 123-136) which now requeries when the cached scopeMap does not contain the requested name/folder. The PR's stated goal — 'dash/folder creator can't access the dashboard/folder that they've just created' — is therefore only fixed for Check; a user who navigates to the dashboards list immediately after creating a dashboard will not see the new entry until the permCache expires (30s). Either List should also requery when the requested name/folder is absent from the cached scopes, or at minimum the dashboard/folder create path should invalidate or refresh the relevant permCache entries.

findings.title: Test comment claims 'allow access' but the value is set to deny
findings.body: In TestService_CacheCheck / 'Should deny on explicit cache deny entry' the comment reads '// Allow access to the dashboard to prove this is not checked' immediately above `s.permCache.Set(ctx, userPermCacheKey(...), map[string]bool{"dashboards:uid:dash1": false})`. The map value is false, so the permCache entry would deny access if it were consulted (the check is `if scopeMap[t.scope(req.Name)]`). The test still passes because the denial cache is hit first, but the comment misrepresents what the permCache entry contains and could mislead anyone reading it. Either set the value to true (to match the comment) or rewrite the comment to say something like '// permCache entry that would allow access — never consulted because the denial cache wins'.
